findings.current: Im Changsoo raised a hand to stop him.
findings.defect: Im Chunsoo’s surname is incorrectly changed to Changsoo.
findings.rationale: This creates an apparent new character in the middle of a scene involving the established Guild Master.
findings.replacement: Im Chunsoo raised a hand to stop him.

findings.current: Im Changsoo went ahead, and I followed behind him.
findings.defect: Im Chunsoo’s surname is incorrectly changed to Changsoo a second time.
findings.rationale: The name must remain consistent with Im Chunsoo throughout the encounter.
findings.replacement: Im Chunsoo went ahead, and I followed behind him.

findings.current: “I’m glad I’m not too late. You too, Chunsoo.”
findings.defect: The repeated dialogue differs from the exact line at the end of Chapter 100.
findings.rationale: Chapter 101 directly replays the same moment, so the line should match Chapter 100 rather than changing its wording and address order.
findings.replacement: “I’m glad I’m not late. Chunsoo, you’re here too.”
findings.source: Chapter 101, opening recap of Kim Hwajong’s arrival

findings.current: Five men were looking this way and snickering.
findings.defect: The opponent count contradicts the chapter’s closing report and checkpoint materials, which consistently state that Taekyung subdued six men.
findings.rationale: The number of aggressors must remain consistent within the chapter and with the summary and active continuity.
findings.replacement: Six men were looking this way and snickering.

findings.current: Wikyung gave Mujin fifty silver nyang for the journey; Mujin has five silver nyang left after paying half the lodging fee.
findings.defect: The summary conflates Mujin’s remaining travel funds with his separate personal savings. After paying twenty-five nyang in advance, he retains twenty-five nyang of the travel funds; the five nyang is his personal emergency savings, already consumed by the meal bill.
findings.rationale: The current statement contradicts the explicit accounting in Chapter 104 and drops the distinction between entrusted travel money and Mujin’s own savings.
findings.replacement: Wikyung gave Mujin fifty silver nyang for the journey; after paying half the lodging fee, Mujin has twenty-five silver nyang of those travel funds left, while the meal has already consumed his five silver nyang in personal emergency savings.

findings.current: After seeing that his spendthrift son had been shaken down for a hundred million won in income, he had started digging into our Guild.
findings.defect: The phrase “a hundred million won in income” incorrectly makes the extorted money sound like income and produces an unnatural collocation.
findings.rationale: Removing “in income” restores the intended causal statement without changing the amount or event.
findings.replacement: After seeing that his spendthrift son had been shaken down for a hundred million won, he had started digging into our Guild.
findings.source: Chapter 100, Taekyung’s interrogation of Kim Junsu

findings.current: Seeing my thoughts written plainly across my face, Butler Kim curled up the corners of his mouth.
findings.defect: “Curled up the corners of his mouth” is an awkward English collocation.
findings.rationale: The replacement conveys the same restrained expression in natural contemporary English.
findings.replacement: Seeing my thoughts written plainly across my face, Butler Kim’s lips curled into a smile.
findings.source: Chapter 101, conversation in Kim Hwajong’s car

summary: The packet is broadly consistent in voice, terminology, hooks, and spoiler control, but it contains two character-name errors, a contradictory opponent count, an incorrect financial continuity note, one mismatched repeated line, and two localized prose defects.
